teaser.text: Ecolab helps organizations keep water usable, workplaces clean and products safe. It earns that role through consumable chemistry, installed equipment, technical service and digital monitoring, then spends the resulting revenue on the people and materials that make those systems work.

blocks.heading: Where could Ecolab's shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: The probability-weighted value is $303.87 in October 2027. That represents a 7% return with dividends. It rises to $335.94 in October 2028, or 19%. By October 2029, the weighted value reaches $371.78, or 33%.

The range is much wider than the weighted path suggests. By October 2029, the bear case gives $195.16, while the bull case gives $590.33. Against today’s $287.89, the forecast assigns 28% to the bear case, 54% to the base case and 18% to the bull case.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Ecolab's forecast?

paragraphs.text: The case turns on customer volume and pricing, CoolIT's contribution, restructuring savings, cash conversion, and the valuation multiple investors will pay. Third-quarter 2026 results, expected October 27, will test the EPS range, pricing, volume, margins, cash collection, and a fuller quarter of CoolIT ownership. Investor Day on November 17, 2026, should test whether cooling becomes deployments, recurring revenue, and profitable growth. CoolIT must become adjusted-EPS accretive in 2028, savings must arrive by 2027, and debt must decline without weakening service.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Ecolab really make?

paragraphs.text: Stock compensation requires another adjustment. Ecolab added it back in operating cash flow because issuing shares requires no immediate cash, but the shares still transfer value to employees. Subtracting $136.6 million of stock pay leaves an analytical “real free cash flow” figure. The recurring test is whether customer programs fund equipment replacement and growth without relying on asset sales or temporary working-capital releases.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Ecolab today?

paragraphs.text: At $287.89 a share, shareholders value Ecolab at $80,703.8 million. Its trailing P/E, the share price divided by one year of earnings per share, is 38.6x: investors pay 38.6 times the latest annual earnings. The forward P/E is 35.3x because it uses expected earnings for the next twelve months. That lower figure already assumes growth, and a later move to 30x would cut the share price about 15% even if earnings met expectations.

blocks.heading: How much does Ecolab pay per share?

paragraphs.text: The base case assumes the quarterly rate rises from $0.73 to $0.79, $0.85 and $0.92, producing payments per share of $3.89, $3.40 and $3.68 across the forecast windows. That is an 8% annual increase, below the latest 12% raise but consistent with Ecolab’s 34-year record of annual increases and $1.9 billion of 2025 free cash flow.

blocks.heading: Is Ecolab's dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: Ecolab generated more cash, but it could not use that cash for every attractive purpose at once. Free cash flow rose from $1,418.9 million in 2021 to $1,904.3 million in 2025, after capital spending on factories and equipment placed with customers. That capital spending itself rose from $643.0 million to $1,048.3 million, so the remainder was not simply surplus.

Dividends were the continuing commitment, reaching $737.1 million in 2025. Buybacks were the adjustable outlet: together, shareholder distributions absorbed 89.9% of free cash flow in 2024 and 79.9% in 2025. That choice benefits owners immediately, but it leaves less cash for acquisitions or debt repayment.

blocks.heading: What has Ecolab guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: Ecolab’s treatment and cleaning programs help customers manage water, energy and equipment. An energy surcharge passes higher commodity costs back to those customers. Management expects total pricing of 5.0%–6.0% from July through December 2026. The increase works only if customers believe Ecolab saves them more than the higher bill costs. A customer may accept a 5% increase if the service cuts water, energy, labour or equipment costs by more than 5%, but volume must be watched because customers can buy less or switch suppliers.

For the full year, management guides to adjusted diluted earnings per share of $8.05–$8.25, up 7.0%–10.0%. Adjusted EPS removes selected special gains, charges and tax items, but this forecast still includes CoolIT’s financing costs and noncash amortization. Amortization records the value of acquired intangible assets over time; financing costs are interest payments on the borrowing used for the acquisition. Management separately expects special charges of $0.75–$0.80 per share.

blocks.heading: Did Ecolab keep its past promise?

paragraphs.text: Management forecast adjusted EPS between US$7.42 and US$7.62 for 2025. It delivered US$7.53. The public promise was therefore met. But the internal incentive target was US$7.27, and the payout on that measure was 137%. Both statements can be true because the forecast and the bonus hurdle were different.

blocks.heading: What should you watch in Ecolab's next results?

paragraphs.text: On October 27, 2026, Ecolab’s third-quarter results should test the adjusted EPS promise of $2.13–$2.23 and provide a fuller quarter of CoolIT ownership. Investors should compare pricing with customer volumes, then examine margins and cash collection. Higher revenue from a larger invoice is less useful if customers are quietly buying less.
